assumptions: The rows are aligned; similarity is summed column by column under the chosen model.
limits: The similarity matrix is not centred, so the first axis often tracks overall similarity rather than a split.
An eigenvalue near zero makes its coordinates huge and meaningless; the eigenvalues are reported so they can be read.
bio.jane/contract.question: How do the rows of this alignment group, on the principal axes of their pairwise similarity?

description: Principal component analysis of the rows of an alignment: the pairwise similarity of every two rows under PID or a substitution matrix (BLOSUM62, PAM250 for protein; Jalview's DNA matrix for nucleotides), decomposed into eigenvectors, and each row's coordinate on the leading components, so rows that cluster sit together. Jalview's PCA, with its parameters: gap–gap and gap–residue columns counted, a gap never matching. Needs 4 rows. Wire `alignedSequences` from align_sequences.

_files.description: The project: record references shaped like _subject. Their records become library documents a tool names in sequences/parts/document; a trace or alignment is found by file name.

_subject.description: The record to act on: exactly one of sequence, accession (+source), sample (an id from list_samples) or file ({name, text} or {name, base64}); record_index picks one record of several.

components.description: how many leading components to report per row.

model.description: the similarity model: PID for any alphabet, BLOSUM62 or PAM250 for protein, DNA for nucleotides. Values: PID (Percent identity), BLOSUM62 (BLOSUM62), PAM250 (PAM250), DNA (DNA).

rows.description: the ALIGNED rows, each {name, aligned}. Wire `alignedSequences` from align_sequences.

name: alignment_pca

coordinates.description: each row's coordinates on the leading components, {name, pc: [PC1, PC2, …]}

similarity.description: the pairwise similarity matrix the analysis decomposed, rows in alignment order

summary.description: the model, the leading eigenvalues and their share of the total
